publications.title: Three Color Suffice: Conflict Free Coloring for Planar Graphs
publications.subtitle: SODA 2017 ACM/SIAM
publications.description: A conflict-free k-coloring of a graph assigns one of k different colors to some of the vertices such that, for every vertex v, there is a color that is assigned to exactly one vertex among v and v’s neighbors. Such colorings have applications in wireless networking, robotics, and geometry, and are well-studied in graph theory.In this paper we present a whole spectrum of results from conflict-free coloring of planar graphs and prove that three colors are always sufficient and sometimes necessary for planar graphs.The paper was accepted in Symposium of Discrete Algorithms 2017.

activity.title: Today marks one year at FurtherAI . Crazy. I was uncomfortable, imposter syndrome kicked in from time to time, and if I’m being honest, I probably regretted making the move at first. But looking back, it was the best decision I’ve made for myself (ever). It wasn’t easy, though. Being at a Series A company is never easy. Every day is different. You wear so many hats, things move fast, it’s scrappy, and there’s rarely a playbook. You figure it out as you go, and I think all of that has shaped me into the person I am today. Scaling AI adoption in insurance is different than any other industry. Arron Lamp explains it best: "If I don't have trustability, if I don't have verifiability, if I can't have something I can put in front of my compliance officer and say, ''We're using AI in our process,'' and have an audit log, I can't use it." When Arron was evaluating AI partners, FurtherAI stood out from the rest. Here’s what he had to say: "They're the only vendor we evaluated that gave us the speed, accuracy, 100%. With no prep, literally no prep. We showed up to our second round saying, ''We want you to do this.'' And they said, ''Actually, we gave you IDs. Why don't you do it?'' Nobody did that." Our Co-Founder and CEO Aman Gour sat down with Arron at InsurTech Insights to talk about how insurance teams should approach AI implementation: "Focus a little bit more on preparing for AI rather than doing AI. Spending time on that will pay huge dividends as you go forward." Full conversation linked in comments! ...more ...more

Insurance has moved through three eras. First, paper. Documentation that humans processed by hand. Then, systems of record. Data lived in a database, but people still entered, moved, and made every decision on top of it. We're in a third era now: systems hold the data, AI agents do the work, and humans apply judgment on what the agents produce. That's agentic insurance: workflows run on AI and moderated by humans. FurtherAI 's Agentic Workspace is built for this era. Start with one workflow — submission intake, claims processing, policy audit — and the integrations, data, and relationships you build compound from there. Our CEO and Co-Founder Aman Gour sat down with Insurance Innovators to talk through what this looks like in practice, and where the industry is heading. Full interview here: ...more ...more

Novacore , an independent specialty insurance provider managing more than $1.5 billion in premium across 20+ programs, chose FurtherAI as their strategic AI partner three weeks ago. Each of those programs runs on underwriting logic its team built over years. That logic is a competitive differentiation worth protecting rather than standardizing away — so the technology has to adapt to how underwriters already work, not the other way around. FurtherAI sits across the portfolio as the orchestration layer, covering submission intake through triage, quoting, and underwriting audits. The architecture adapts to how each team already operates, and that same foundation carries into every new program and company Novacore brings in. Aaron Miller , Chief Executive Officer at Novacore, put the result this way: "FurtherAI gives us data centralization, orchestration, and a true intelligence layer across our business." Less time chasing details, more time on risk selection. Thank you to Aaron, Joe Christman , and the Novacore team. Full story here: https://lnkd.in/emCDxk4k ...more ...more

Partnering with FurtherAI allows us to leverage insurance-specific AI to remove manual friction from our claims processes, ultimately enabling our teams to focus on what matters most: supporting our members." - Ed Yeung , SVP Insurance Solutions, RMA Thank you to Anthony, Ed, and the entire RMA team. ...more ...more

Insurance work lives across dozens of disconnected systems and AI is only as useful as the context it has access to. Today, we're launching the FurtherAI Connectors, bringing together the tools and data sources that power modern insurance operations. Connect CRMs like Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics. Policy admin systems like Guidewire, Duck Creek, and Majesco. AMS platforms like Applied Epic, AMS360, Sagitta, and EZLynx. Document systems like SharePoint and ImageRight. Plus enrichment sources including OSHA, OFAC, HazardHub, BuildZoom, Trellis, PitchBook, Google, and more. With a single connection, teams can pull documents, data, and institutional knowledge directly into FurtherAI workflows without jumping between systems. The result is faster implementations, richer context, and AI that works the way insurance teams do. This is the foundation for building an Agentic Workspace for insurance. More connectors are coming soon. ...more ...more

Most people begin by using AI to do their existing work a little faster. Better personal productivity. A few minutes saved here and there. That is a reasonable starting point, but it is not where the greatest value lies. The bigger opportunity comes when we stop asking only how to complete the same work faster and start asking how the work itself should change. Less, “How can I write this document 20% faster?” More, “If AI can perform part of this work, how should we redesign the process, the role, or the customer experience?” At Travelers, code reviews that once took days can now be completed in hours and, in some cases, minutes. The productivity benefit is meaningful. But the bigger opportunity is what that makes possible: more time for difficult design decisions, deeper collaboration with the business, and greater focus on the problems that require human judgment. Automation improves individual steps. Transformation reimagines the full flow of work. We need both. But the most enduring value will come from being willing to redesign the work, not simply accelerate the way it has always been done. #TravelersTech #AI #Transformation
